key_insight: REST3D reconstructs 3D scenes from a single RGB image while explicitly enforcing physical stability, producing simulation-ready, collision-free scene geometry instead of merely visually plausible meshes.
problem_solved: Existing single-image 3D reconstruction methods often produce geometrically believable but physically inconsistent scenes (floating objects, interpenetration, unstable stacks) that fail in simulators; this work addresses the gap between visual fidelity and physical plausibility.
method: Decompose the scene into objects and support relationships, predicting per-object geometry and poses from a single image.
Incorporate physics-aware objectives (differentiable stability/contact losses or a differentiable simulator) during reconstruction to penalize penetrations and unstable configurations.
Jointly optimize geometry, poses, and contact constraints to produce collision-free meshes and physically stable arrangements ready for simulation.
impact: Enables conversion of casual images into reliable, simulation-ready 3D assets for robotics, AR/VR, and content creation workflows; reduces manual cleanup and improves downstream physics-based reasoning and interaction.
visual_elements: Before/After comparison: reconstructed scene without physics (floating/penetrating) vs. REST3D stable reconstruction.
Pipeline diagram: single RGB input → object decomposition → physics-aware optimization → simulation-ready scene.
Stability visualization: contact/force arrows or heatmap showing where support and load are distributed between objects.
Simulation frames or short animation: reconstructed scene undergoing physics stepping to show stable behavior (no collapse or interpenetration).
paper_title: REST3D: Reconstructing Physically Stable 3D Scenes from a Single Image
paper_authors: Xiaoxuan Ma, Jiashun Wang, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Yehonathan Litman, Kris Kitani
